name: Recruit Training Command, Great Lakes
explanation: Enlisted boot camp for the Navy, at Naval Station Great Lakes, Illinois. Recruit training was 10 weeks in September 1997.
civilian: This is where a new sailor learns to live in the Navy before going on to a technical school.

name: USS Tortuga (LSD-46)
explanation: A Whidbey Island-class dock landing ship. It carries Marines with their vehicles and landing craft, and launches the craft from a well deck that floods. The dates of this assignment have not been entered.
civilian: A ship that carries Marines and their boats and vehicles to a beach.

name: Naval Training Center Great Lakes
explanation: The Navy's training center at Great Lakes, Illinois. The emblem shown is the seal of Naval Station Great Lakes, the installation's current name. The dates of this assignment have not been entered.
open: NTC Great Lakes: dates not entered.
civilian: The Navy's big training base north of Chicago.

name: Naval Computer and Telecommunications Station San Diego
explanation: A shore command that ran Navy computer and telecommunications services in San Diego. The shadowbox lists the NEC for this tour as 1589, calibration.
civilian: A land-based communications station, not a ship.

name: USS Frank Cable (AS-40)
explanation: A submarine tender: a ship that repairs, supplies, and houses the crews of submarines. In these years her home port was Guam. The NEC on the shadowbox for this tour is 1589. The three Navy E awards dated 2001, 2002, and 2003 fall in this tour.
civilian: A repair ship for submarines, not a submarine itself.

name: EOD Mobile Unit Five
explanation: Explosive Ordnance Disposal Mobile Unit Five, a Navy bomb-disposal unit then based in Guam. Assignment to the unit is not the same as being a bomb-disposal technician. The shadowbox lists the NEC as 9613, a communications specialty.
civilian: The command's job was disposing of explosives. His recorded specialty there was communications.

name: Combined Joint Task Force Troy
explanation: A joint and coalition task force in Iraq in 2006, during Operation Iraqi Freedom, stood up against roadside bombs. The shadowbox lists it as a 2006 assignment with NEC 9613, inside the EOD Mobile Unit Five years. The Iraq campaign phase named for this tour is National Resolution.
civilian: A temporary headquarters in Iraq, drawn from more than one country and more than one branch.

name: 52nd Ordnance Group (EOD)
explanation: A U.S. Army explosive ordnance disposal group. Joint/attached service; the role and dates have not been entered.
open: 52nd Ordnance Group (EOD): role and dates not entered.

name: 16th Engineer Brigade
explanation: A U.S. Army engineer brigade, recorded as 16th EN. Joint/attached service; the role and dates have not been entered.
open: 16th Engineer Brigade: role and dates not entered.

name: 3rd Special Forces Group (Airborne)
explanation: A U.S. Army Special Forces group. Joint/attached service; the role and dates have not been entered. Shown with the Special Forces shoulder sleeve insignia and the 3rd Group beret flash.
open: 3rd Special Forces Group: role and dates not entered.

name: 75th Ranger Regiment
explanation: The U.S. Army's Ranger regiment. Joint/attached service; the role and dates have not been entered.
open: 75th Ranger Regiment: role and dates not entered.

name: Southeast Regional Calibration Center
explanation: The Navy's Southeast Regional Calibration Center, at Naval Air Station Jacksonville. A calibration center checks the test equipment other commands use. The NEC on this tour is 1589, which matches that work.
civilian: A laboratory that keeps measuring tools honest.

name: 11th Air Defense Artillery Brigade (IA)
explanation: An individual augmentee is a sailor loaned to another service for a deployment. This one was to the Army, in Iraq, with NEC ET-0000, meaning no extra specialty code. The campaign phase named for this tour is Iraq Sovereignty. The Army unit was the 11th Air Defense Artillery Brigade. The collection includes a challenge coin from Task Force C-RAM, 3rd Battalion, 3rd Air Defense Artillery (3-3 ADA).
civilian: He was still a sailor, working inside an Army deployment.

name: Joint Communications Support Element
explanation: A joint unit, based at MacDill Air Force Base in Florida, that sends small communications teams out quickly for special operations and other joint commanders. The shadowbox dates the tour 2009–2015 and lists NEC 9613. It included the two Afghanistan deployments.
civilian: A communications unit made of every branch, not a Navy ship.

name: Combined Joint Special Operations Task Force — Afghanistan
explanation: A joint special-operations headquarters in Afghanistan during Operation Enduring Freedom. The shadowbox lists it under the JCSE years, 2010–2011. The role in the record is communications, not service as a special operator.
civilian: The headquarters he supported. Being the communicator for that headquarters is not the same job as the operators it commanded.

name: Naval Hospital Jacksonville
explanation: The Navy hospital at Jacksonville, Florida, and the last active-duty command. Last duty assignment was Naval Hospital Jacksonville, with separation processing at the personnel support detachment on Naval Air Station Jacksonville.
civilian: A hospital, not a ship. An electronics technician there maintains medical and other electronic equipment. The day-to-day job is not further described.
